title: Machine Learning Algorithm Accurately Predicts Mental Health Crises
content:
Koa Health, in collaboration with Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, developed a machine learning model capable of predicting mental health crises from electronic health records up to 28 days in advance.

The study

The research, published in Nature Medicine (Volume 28, Issue 6, June 2022), analysed anonymised electronic health records collected over seven years from NHS Trust patients. The model continuously monitors patients for crisis risk over a 28-day window, identifying patterns that precede a mental health crisis.

Publication: Machine learning model to predict mental health crises from electronic health records — Nature Medicine, DOI: 10.1038/s41591-022-01811-5

Results

  • AUROC of 0.797 and area under the precision-recall curve of 0.159
  • Predicted crises with a sensitivity of 58% at a specificity of 85%
  • A 6-month prospective study found predictions to be clinically valuable in 64% of cases — either for managing caseloads or mitigating crisis risk
  • Described as the first study to continuously predict the risk of a wide range of mental health crises and to evaluate the added clinical value of such predictions

Why it matters

Mental health crises are often preceded by subtle signals that are difficult to detect in time. By surfacing patterns at scale from existing EHR data, this model shifts the model from reactive crisis response to proactive, preventative care — reducing harm and improving outcomes for vulnerable NHS patients.

Further reading

Full technical findings are available in the Nature Medicine paper and on the Koa Health blog.
